subject: Cheaper gold, dearer plate: the leader’s argument
alt: Subhani’s cartoon: at the left stands an elderly couple; the woman in a red sari and black blouse, wearing glasses, holds her husband’s arm; the man in a white kurta and dhoti with a white shawl on his shoulder, also in glasses, carries a white bag marked with a triangle. At the centre stands a stout leader in a white kurta and dhoti with a brown sleeveless jacket and white shawls round his neck, round glasses and a moustache; he points a finger at the couple and holds papers in his left hand. Behind him stands a man in a black suit, white shirt and red tie, holding papers. Behind them a three-storey building carries boards reading ‘GOLD’, ‘GOLD SHOP’ and ‘SILVER’; a red car stands at the right. At the lower right a card reads ‘GOLD PRICES ↓’. The leader’s bubble reads: ‘RICE, VEGETABLES COSTLY? YOU SHOULD BE HAPPY THAT GOLD AND SILVER ARE CHEAPER’. Subhani’s signature is at the lower left.
chutki: The elderly couple stands with its bag, and the leader points a finger at them: ‘Rice, vegetables costly? You should be happy that gold and silver are cheaper.’ Behind them are shop boards for ‘Gold’ and ‘Silver’, and a card below reads ‘Gold prices ↓’.
The needle: the consolation of cheaper gold is offered to a household whose plate has become dearer. Falling jewellery prices do not fix the kitchen budget.
